latest_release.name: Codewhale v0.10.4
latest_release.body:
## What's in v0.10.4


Codewhale v0.10.4 is a hotfix release. Ctrl+V no longer pastes text twice in Windows Terminal, which also doubled API keys pasted into `/provider`; the fix was checked on a real Windows Terminal. `codewhale update` no longer refuses a release binary because an unrelated `cargo install` left a Cargo record beside it. The refusal happens inside the installed 0.10.3, so an install it affects cannot update itself to 0.10.4: rerun the installer once (`curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or `install.bat` from the 0.10.4 Windows archive), and later updates work. `/provider` now works for projects on a second Windows drive such as D:, Computer Use installs from the Marketplace, and every terminal draws the dot whale in `/pet`. `url` is updated to 2.5.9 for RUSTSEC-2026-0592. DeepSeek Harness compatibility is limited: of 32 published packages tried unmodified, 2 activate in the terminal; [DSH compatibility](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md) lists each one.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.4" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release. Both contain the same compiled runtime.

### Docker / GHCR

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  -v codewhale-home:/home/codewhale/.codewhale \
  ghcr.io/codewhale-hq/codewhale:v0.10.4
```

The image exposes the same runtime as both `codewhale` and `codew`. The
`latest` tag is also updated on release.

### Cargo (Linux / macOS)

```bash
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The Cargo package installs `codewhale`. Cargo cannot create a second command
alias from one binary target; users who want the shorter spelling can add a
`codew` symlink to that installed executable. The npm, Homebrew, archive,
shell-installer, and container channels install both command names directly.

### Manual download — platform archives (recommended)

Each archive below contains the same runtime under the `codewhale` and
`codew` command names, plus an install script:

| Platform | Archive | Install script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `codewhale-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Linux ARM64 | `codewhale-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Android ARM64 (Termux) | `codewhale-android-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| HarmonyOS ARM64 (native) | `codewhale-ohos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS x64 | `codewhale-macos-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS ARM | `codewhale-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Windows x64 (installer) | `CodeWhaleSetup.exe` | NSIS setup |
| Windows x64 | `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows x64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-x64-portable.zip` | — |
| Windows ARM64 | `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows ARM64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-arm64-portable.zip` | — |

**Unix (Linux / macOS):**
```bash
tar xzf codewhale-<platform>.tar.gz
cd codewhale-<platform>
./install.sh
```

**Windows:**
- For the installer path, run `CodeWhaleSetup.exe`; it installs
  `codewhale.exe`, `codew.exe`, and `codewhale.bat` under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin`, adds that directory to the
  current-user PATH, and creates a Start Menu shortcut that prefers
  Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) when it is installed.

detail.readme:
The model can be anyone's. The agent should be yours.

Codewhale is an open-source coding agent for your terminal, written in Rust. It works with any model, can split one task across several agents, and every line of it is yours to read. ```bash curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh ``` This installs the latest release on macOS or Linux, and it needs no account. [Windows, npm and Cargo](#install) are below. [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/codewhale-hq/Codewhale?label=release)](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/releases/latest) [![CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE) [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Discord-join-5865F2?logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/37gfS3ksug) [Website](https://codewhale.net) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) [简体中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-CN.md) · [日本語](docs/i18n/README.ja-JP.md) · [Tiếng Việt](docs/i18n/README.vi.md) · [Bahasa Indonesia](docs/i18n/README.id.md) · [한국어](docs/i18n/README.ko-KR.md) · [Español](docs/i18n/README.es-419.md) · [Português](docs/i18n/README.pt-BR.md) · [Русский](docs/i18n/README.ru.md) · [Українська](docs/i18n/README.uk.md) · [Français](docs/i18n/README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](docs/i18n/README.de.md) · [繁體中文](docs/i18n/README.zh-TW.md) · [हिन्दी](docs/i18n/README.hi.md) · [Türkçe](docs/i18n/README.tr.md) · [Italiano](docs/i18n/README.it.md) · [Polski](docs/i18n/README.pl.md) · [العربية](docs/i18n/README.ar.md) · [Català](docs/i18n/README.ca.md) A real session on a 0.10.3 development build: deepseek-flash through DeepSeek's API wrote the edit, and you allowed the test run once.
## Install The command above puts checksum-verified `codewhale` and its short alias `codew` in `~/.local/bin`. If your shell then says `command not found`, follow the PATH note the installer prints ([details](docs/INSTALL.md#put-it-on-your-path)). `codewhale update` upgrades it. ```bash winget install --id HunterBown.CodeWhale --exact --source winget # Windows x64 npm install -g codewhale # wraps the same release binaries cargo install codewhale-cli --locked # builds from source; can trail GitHub Releases ``` Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, macOS and Windows on x64 and arm64. Scoop, Nix, Homebrew on Linux, Android and Termux (preview) and manual downloads are in the [installation guide](docs/INSTALL.md), and containers are in [Docker](docs/DOCKER.md). Use one install method per machine; otherwise two copies end up on your `PATH` and whichever comes first wins. ## Quickstart 1. Commit or stash your work, then run `codewhale` from the root of a git repository. By default it applies file edits there without asking and asks before each shell command that is not read-only. 2. Run `/provider` (or press `F3`), pick a provider, paste its API key and choose a model. DeepSeek is the default provider. On a first launch with no key, Codewhale asks for a provider when you send your first message, and it offers a local model when a local Ollama server answers. 3. Type a task: ```text Fix the failing tests and explain what changed. ``` Read-only commands run straight away. For any other shell command Codewhale asks first: `y` runs it once, `a` allows commands like it for the rest of the conversation, and `n` refuses. `/undo` takes back your last request and its file changes, and `/help` lists commands and keys. For scripts and CI, `codewhale exec` runs one task without the interface. Read [headless runs](docs/INSTALL.md#headless-scripts-ci) before you give it tools with `--auto`, because `--auto` uses Full Access unless you add a sandbox. ## What it does Give Codewhale a task and it reads the repository, edits files and runs commands until the task is done or it needs your input. The [latest release notes](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/releases/latest) list the newest changes, and the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) has every version. ### Any model More than 40 providers are built in, including Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Google, Mistral, Moonshot, OpenRouter and xAI. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, and so do local models through Ollama, vLLM or SGLang. The default model is DeepSeek's `deepseek-flash`, which now serves DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ([details](docs/PROVIDERS.md#deepseek-v41-flash)). `/model` switches models between turns, and `/model auto` picks one for each turn (`/router` sets up how). `/turn inspect` shows which model a turn used, what it cost and how long it took. See [Providers](docs/PROVIDERS.md). ### Receipts and undo `/receipts`, or `codewhale receipts --last` after you quit, lists the files a session changed, the commands it ran, its web and MCP calls, the agents it started, each approval and who gave it, and what failed. `/undo` takes back your last request and the files it changed in one step. `/restore` rolls the whole workspace back to an earlier snapshot, and because that overwrites later edits it needs `/trust on` or Full Access. See [Receipts](docs/RECEIPTS.md). ### Several agents on one task `/goal` sets an objective that carries across turns. Codewhale can split work across [sub-agents](docs/SUBAGENTS.md), run a [Fleet](docs/FLEET.md) of agents with their own roles and models, or follow a [workflow](docs/WORKFLOW_AUTHORING.md) checked into the repository. ### Plugins Connect [MCP servers](docs/MCP.md), add [skills](docs/SKILLS.md) and [plugins](docs/PLUGINS.md), and run [hooks](docs/HOOKS.md) on session and tool events. Code mode (experimental, on by default) lets the model write one `execute_tools` program that calls several MCP and plugin tools; each call still meets your approval rules and keeps its receipt. [Computer Use](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale-cu-plugin) is a separate plugin released on its own (experimental, macOS only), and stays off until you review its access and turn it on. ### Ways to run it | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `codewhale` | The interactive terminal app | | `codewhale exec "…"` | One task without the interface, for scripts and CI ([headless runs](docs/INSTALL.md#headless-scripts-ci)) | | `codewhale web` | A local web client on `127.0.0.1` ([guide](docs/WEB.md)) | | `codewhale review --pr N` | An advisory review of a GitHub pull request; the [GitHub bot setup](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md#set-up-your-own-bot) runs it on your own model key | | `codewhale app-server --http` | The [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md), a local HTTP API for threads, events, approvals and each turn's file changes | | `codewhale serve --acp` | The Agent Client Protocol over stdio, for editors such as Zed | The terminal app, `exec`, `web` and the Runtime API share one engine ([architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)). A community-maintained [VS Code extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=HengQuWorld.brotherwhale-vscode) connects to it from the sidebar ([source](https://github.com/HengQuWorld/CodeWhale-VSCode)). ## How it stays safe One dial says how much Codewhale may do on its own. `Shift+Tab` steps it: **Ask → Accept Edits → Plan → Auto-Review → Full Access**. **Accept Edits**, the default, applies file edits inside the git repository without asking and asks before commands. **Ask** asks before every file edit and every command. **Plan** reads and searches but changes nothing. **Auto-Review** lets rules and a reviewer model approve routine calls and refuses high-risk ones; switch to Ask to approve those yourself. **Full Access** never asks and turns off Codewhale's sandbox, although repository rules and managed policy still apply. `Tab` only completes and never changes the mode, and Operate is retired. The [modes guide](docs/MODES.md) has the details. In Ask, Accept Edits and Auto-Review, commands run in an OS sandbox where the system has one: Seatbelt on macOS, and bubblewrap on Linux when it is installed. Windows has no OS sandbox yet, and Full Access turns the sandbox off. Inside the sandbox, shell commands and terminal sessions cannot read credential stores such as `~/.ssh`, `~/.aws` and `.env` files. `/preview-request` shows a redacted preview of the next request without sending it. You need no account, and keys you add with `/provider` stay on your machine. With your own API key you pay the provider directly, and local models need no key. The footer and `/cost` show what a session has cost when the price is known, and an unknown price is shown as unknown, never as free. Telemetry is on by default. It sends aggregate counts (version and platform, session length and outcome, which built-in providers you used, feature and error counts) with a random install ID that rotates every 90 days, and never conversations, code, prompts, model names, file or repository names, or credentials. This command turns it off: ```bash codewhale config set telemetry false ``` At startup Codewhale also checks GitHub for a new release; set `CODEWHALE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` to skip that. More in [authorization order](docs/AUTHORIZATION_ORDER.md), [sandboxing](docs/SANDBOX.md) and [telemetry](docs/TELEMETRY.md). ## Where it is going Codewhale is becoming one environment across your terminal, a desktop app, the browser and cloud computers, all run by one engine. Each part says where it stands today. | Part | State | Today | | --- | --- | --- | | Terminal app | Released | Install it on macOS, Linux or Windows and run `codewhale` in any repository. | | Local browser client | Released | Run `codewhale web` to read the conversation, send a task and answer approvals in your browser; it comes with the terminal and needs no account. | | Many agents on one task | Released | Sub-agents, Fleets and workflows let several agents share one task, each with its own role. | | Desktop app | In development, no download | We are building a desktop app on the same engine, and it has no public download yet. | | Cloud computers | Invite-only | Cloud computers are invite-only, and we are building them so a session can keep working on a machine in the cloud. | | One session across them | Being built | We are building one session that goes with you from the terminal to the desktop, the browser and the cloud, and stays yours the whole way. | The [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) says what each release covers and where you can help. ## Coming from another agent Codewhale reads `AGENTS.md` on its own. Instruction files written for other tools, such as `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` or `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, load only when you opt in with `project_instruction_imports = ["claude"]` (or `"cursor"`, `"cline"`, `"windsurf"`, `"copilot"`, `"all"`) in your config; see [config.example.toml](config.example.toml). Codewhale warns when it finds one it did not load. `/import-claude` prepares an import of your Claude Code settings and MCP servers for you to review. `/plugin install` accepts Claude Code plugins that contain skills, commands, agent profiles and MCP servers, and refuses plugins that need hooks or LSP servers ([details](docs/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_COMPAT.md)). ## Documentation These guides follow the main branch and can describe changes that are not in the latest release yet. | Start here | Reference | | --- | --- | | [User guide](docs/GUIDE.md) | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) | | [Installation](docs/INSTALL.md) | [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | | [Providers and local models](docs/PROVIDERS.md) | [Runtime API](docs/RUNTIME_API.md) | | [Modes and permissions](docs/MODES.md) | [Plugin authoring](docs/PLUGIN_AUTHORING.md) | | [Keybindings](docs/KEYBINDINGS.md) | [Receipts](docs/RECEIPTS.md) | | [GitHub pull request review](docs/GITHUB_ACTION.md) | [All documentation](docs/README.md) | ## Contributing Codewhale is built in the open by the people who use it, in many languages. The [contributor wall](docs/CONTRIBUTORS.md) counts everyone whose code, co-authored commits, carried-forward pull requests or credited reports are in Codewhale, including people GitHub's own contributor list misses. `scripts/contributor-wall.py` regenerates the picture and the list from git history and GitHub. All feedback is welcome: a bug, an idea, or something that looked or felt wrong. [Open an issue](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/new/choose) for any of these; an issue is also the best place to start a new feature. Pull requests are welcome for fixes, translations, providers and planned work. Questions go to [Discussions](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/discussions). The [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) shows where each kind of help goes, how your work lands with your name on it, and [where things live](CONTRIBUTING.md#project-structure). Chat on [Discord](https://discord.gg/37gfS3ksug), or add the maintainer, Hunter, on WeChat (`hunterbown`) and ask to join the Whale Brothers group. Everyone is welcome. ## History and license Codewhale started as `deepseek-tui` and still reads that project's configuration and sessions. It is independently maintained and not affiliated with DeepSeek or any other model provider. [MIT](LICENSE). Code adapted from other open-source projects is listed in the third-party notices for [vendored sources](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [adapted designs](docs/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).
